newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 5.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Kirton verdict increases tension: Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton has been cleared of wrongdoing in a draft report from the auditor-general -- further straining his working relationship with Health Minister Bill English, who requested the probe. Page 1.

NZ First rolls out big guns to debate super scheme: Senior NZ First MPs are upping the ante in debate over the compulsory superannuation scheme championed by their leader Winston Peters, with a series of speeches urging its support despite polls suggesting the cause may already by lost. Page 2.

Rabbit virus parties must wait for review: Parties seeking a review of the rabbit-killing calicivirus decision would have to wait at least another two weeks for an answer to their request, the Agriculture Ministry said on Monday. Page 2.

Board to sell juice arm to focus on marketing: The Apple and Pear Board is shedding Frucor Beverages, the biggest seller of fruit juice in New Zealand, to get back to its central business of the international market of pip fruit. Page 13.
CBD vacancy rates static, survey finds: Wellington businesses virtually stopped taking on more office space during the past six months, according to Ernst and Young. Page 13.

Label proposal upsets Manfed: Government ministers were "crawling" to please Australia over country-of-origin labelling rules, Manufacturers Federation chief executive Simon Arnold said on Monday. Page 13.
THE PRESS

Call to sack Kirton over contract: Labour may attempt to haul Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton before the powerful privileges committee for allegedly misleading Parliament over the awarding of an advertising contract to a firm headed by a relative. Page 1.
Privatisation plan leaked: Tertiary education would be privatised under secret government plans, Labour says. Page 7.

Kiwi slides as RB stands by MCI: The Reserve Bank stood by its position on monetary conditions as the New Zealand dollar continued its slide from last week and interest rates failed to rise sufficiently to compensate. Page 33.

RB sees little scope for easing if RSS adopted: Any easing in monetary policy following a yes vote in next month's compulsory Retirement Savings Scheme (RSS) referendum would be small, the Reserve Bank's chief manager of financial markets, David Archer, said on Monday. Page 33.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Now it's competition on campus: Study vouchers for students -- and universities and polytechs designed to make money -- are key proposals in a secret government briefing paper urging radical changes to the country's tertiary system.
Senior executives to go into TVNZ revamp: Two more senior executives are leaving TVNZ and more are expected to follow as the corporation's management undergoes a shake-up.

Egerton to try again on regional TV: Former TVNZ and TV3 executive Trevor Egerton is understood to have teamed up with a subsidiary of Australia's Channel 7 to relaunch regional television in New Zealand.
Govt moving to plug loophole: The government is planning to plug what it sees as a leak in the tax base by legislating to ensure inducements to enter into leases are treated as taxable income.
BellSouth baulks at academic's warning: BellSouth is bitting back at suggestions by an Otago University academic that its GSM digital mobile-phone service might not be secure.
Baker confident new look will pay in long run: Delays to Christchurch-based baker Ernest Adams Ltd's restructuring plans in 1996 failed to boost paltry profits.
